title: CUDA stream stall & prefetch race condition: scaling review - Elara Bio
action_items: Nina Ko: share 3-days worth of agent logs + nvprof output (due 2026-08-18)
Luis Ortega: provide a reproducer script that toggles prefetch concurrency and batch windows (due 2026-08-13)
Iris Patel: draft recommended allocator/env var settings for on-prem nodes (due 2026-08-16)
next_steps: Redwood SE to run reproducer on dedicated test GPU cluster and return traces
Schedule on-prem PoC for throughput runs week of 2026-08-24
AE to share security checklist and draft commercial term sheet for dedicated capacity
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, want to get right into the stream stalls you've been seeing in your pre-prod cluster. can you describe the high level outage pattern one more time Tomas?
[00:18] Tomás Rivera: yeah so, over the last two weeks we had these intermittent stalls where the host shows the job as active but the token throughput drops to zero for 10-30s then resumes. it's worse under mixed sequence workloads, when some requests are 2k tokens and some are 32.
[00:36] Luis Ortega: and just to add we saw a correlation with the new prefetcher patch you rolled — the prefetch concurrency default was bumped from 2 to 6. when concurrency is high, streams seem to block.
[00:48] Nina Ko: we thought it was a kernel bug at first but after pinning to an older kernel the behavior persisted. we also see a spike in device-side CUDA errors: "cudaErrorLaunchTimeout" and occasional OOMs even though absolute memory usage looks under threshold.
[01:05] Luis Ortega: that matches a stream stall pattern where a pending callback never completes and the runtime queues up more work; memory allocs fragment so a subsequent workspace allocation fails and triggers an OOM. it's subtle.
[01:22] Rajesh Singh: is this related to KV cache? we turned on aggressive KV prefetch so when a prompt asks for long context we prefetch keys for the full prefix.
[01:30] Iris Patel: yes KV cache (we called it k v cash in ev logs) appears in traces. we noticed prefetch tasks spawn their own CUDA streams and sometimes race with the main inference stream for cuBLAS/cuDNN handles.
[01:46] Luis Ortega: exactly — our runtime spawns a small pool of helper streams for prefetch/eviction; if the device scheduler mis-orders or a prefetch blocks on host pinned memory we can hit a deadlock-like stall.
[02:00] Maya Chen: ok, what telemetry do you have? Nina?
[02:04] Nina Ko: logs: attached a few timestamps where the infer loop waited 24s for a stream callback. we also have nvprof traces for two runs: one with prefetch concurrency 2 (stable) and one with 6 (unstable). I'll upload after this call.
[02:18] Luis Ortega: great — we'll want the nvprof/NSYS timeline; look for stream synchronization points, cudaMemcpyAsync overheads, and whether the prefetch kernels block on small synchronous memcpys.
[02:30] Tomás Rivera: also note this happens more on our on-prem racks. cloud hosts (GCP) show fewer incidents. could be driver differences or kernel params.
[02:39] Iris Patel: we're on Ubuntu 20.04 with 510 driver on-prem; GCP is 525. different CUDA runtime versions, and our allocator settings are default.
[02:50] Luis Ortega: allocator is important. the default device malloc and fragmentation from quantized kernels can create big headroom loss, especially with int8 kernels that do scratch/permutation buffers.
[03:02] Nina Ko: re: quantization — we rolled LLM-quant-v2 for several models. after quantization we actually observed more frequent small allocations (permutes, reorder workspace) and that seems to expose fragmentation.
[03:15] Rajesh Singh: so quant is making it worse. if we roll back to fp16 do stalls reduce?
[03:20] Luis Ortega: generally yes; quantized backends sometimes need temporary buffers that are allocated per-layer on the device and freed later — if prefetching increases concurrency you get many small allocations in flight.
[03:32] Maya Chen: let's talk retries. we've seen retry storms where the client retries and duplicates inflight requests causing more pressure. what does your client retry policy look like?
[03:41] Tomás Rivera: our service retries at the LB layer with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts, but we don't use idempotency tokens so duplicates are not deduped.
[03:51] Iris Patel: duplicates amplify the tail because the runtime isn't de-duplicating identical KV prefetch work. so the prefetcher will schedule the same keys multiple times, increasing concurrent memory footprints.
[04:02] Luis Ortega: two-pronged mitigation: 1) enforce idempotency at API edge and dedupe prefetch tasks; 2) limit prefetch concurrency and add async cancellation for prefetch tasks when an inference cancels.
[04:15] Nina Ko: cancellation is hard — our code path doesn't propagate a cancel token from the LB to the driver level. we rely on soft timeouts right now.
[04:23] Luis Ortega: soft timeouts don't free device buffers; you need to ensure we call the runtime free path and drain any pending streams. we can add a cancel token in the next runtime release but that will require on-prem upgrades.
[04:35] Tomás Rivera: what about batching? we're using dynamic batching windows of 30ms. could that interact with the prefetch race?
[04:43] Luis Ortega: yes, the batcher coalesces requests which increases per-batch workspace size. if a slow request with 2k tokens enters a batch with many short requests, the runtime may allocate a large intermediate buffer then stall waiting for the long request's KV resolution; prefetch expands memory pressure.
[04:59] Maya Chen: any quick mitigations you can deploy on-prem while you wait for runtime changes?
[05:03] Luis Ortega: immediate mitigations: reduce prefetch_concurrency to 1-2, set batch_max_tokens cap, enable KV cache LRU eviction threshold lower (e.g., 60% of device memory), and set GPU_PERF_WORKAROUND env to throttle helper streams. Also disable aggressive quantization scratch until we roll allocator patches.
[05:22] Nina Ko: can you share exact env var names and settings?
[05:25] Luis Ortega: yes — I'll paste in the runbook. key ones: REDWOOD_PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=2, REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=8192, REDWOOD_KV_EVICTION_HIGH_WATER=0.6, REDWOOD_HELPER_STREAM_THROTTLE=0.25, REDWOOD_QUANT_SCRATCH_DISABLE=true. these are suggestions and some names are shorthand — your infra team will map them to actual flags.
[05:48] Iris Patel: we prefer changes that don't require restarting the entire node. can these be patched at runtime?
[05:53] Luis Ortega: most are dynamic config toggles hitting the config manager, some require restart only when changing allocator strategy. prefetch_concurrency, eviction watermarks, and batch caps can be changed live.
[06:03] Rajesh Singh: what about driver-level fixes? should we upgrade to 525 across the on-prem fleet?
[06:09] Luis Ortega: upgrading helps — newer drivers fix stream scheduling and memcpy async bugs. but driver upgrades have their own compatibility risks. we recommended a staged canary: upgrade 1 rack and run the reproducer before fleet-wide rollouts.
[06:20] Maya Chen: in terms of long-term runtime fixes what are Redwood engineers planning?
[06:24] Luis Ortega: plan is threefold: 1) protective allocator with defragmenting freelist and per-stream arenas to reduce head fragmentation; 2) prefetch task deduplication and cancel tokens; 3) stronger backpressure in batcher so we don't schedule huge ephemeral scratch for short tail requests.
[06:41] Nina Ko: timeline?
[06:43] Luis Ortega: prototyping allocator changes now, aiming for a minor release in ~6 weeks and GA in ~10–12 weeks. dedupe and cancel tokens in a following patch ~8 weeks.
[06:53] Tomás Rivera: for the PoC can you simulate our mixed workload and then reproduce the stall locally?
[06:57] Luis Ortega: yes — that's the reproducer I'll send, it toggles quantization on/off, varies prefetch concurrency, reproduces mixed sequence length distribution, and captures NSYS.
[07:08] Maya Chen: ok, let's capture concrete next steps and owners.
[07:11] Rajesh Singh: quick question — are there any risks with lowering KV eviction threshold? could that cause evict thrashing?
[07:18] Luis Ortega: yes if set too low you'll evict frequently which raises I/O overhead; recommended to tune incrementally — start at 60% then watch eviction rate, hit ratio, and latency 95 percentiles.
[07:29] Nina Ko: we'll be careful. also we need to confirm compliance impact of sending NVPROF traces to Redwood — we'll scrub artifacts first.
[07:36] Maya Chen: understood. we'll accept scrubbed traces. Iris will coordinate the secure upload link.
[07:43] Luis Ortega: one more note on retries: implement idempotency tokens at the LB and add a small jitter to backoff so retries don't synchronize. also add server-side dedupe for prefetch tasks keyed by (model, prefix hash).
[07:56] Tomás Rivera: can Redwood detect and auto-throttle helper streams if a stall is detected?
[08:01] Luis Ortega: there's a watchdog we can enable that monitors stream progress; if a helper stream hasn't made progress in N seconds it can preempt and move work back to main stream or requeue with backoff. that's part of the protective runtime work.
[08:15] Maya Chen: good. let's wrap up with confirmation of action items and dates.
[08:19] Maya Chen: Luis to send reproducer and sample nsys capture commands by 2026-08-13.
[08:23] Luis Ortega: yep will do.
[08:25] Maya Chen: Nina to upload scrubbed nvprof traces and logs by 2026-08-18.
[08:29] Nina Ko: yes.
[08:30] Maya Chen: Iris will coordinate secure upload link and confirm driver versions across racks by 2026-08-15.
[08:35] Iris Patel: will do.
[08:36] Maya Chen: I'll schedule the on-prem PoC kickoff for week of 2026-08-24.
[08:40] Rajesh Singh: thanks everybody, appreciated.
[08:42] Maya Chen: thanks, bye.
[08:43] End of recording.
